# StateLine Calc

> Free US paycheck and take-home pay calculators, state by state, for tax year 2026.
> Every rate is read from the agency that sets it and published with the date it was
> checked. Nothing a visitor types leaves their browser.

StateLine Calc answers one question precisely: what actually reaches your bank account
from a given gross salary or hourly rate, in a given US state, in 2026. Each state page
carries the answer three ways: a calculator, a 14-row table of common salaries, and a
14-row table of common hourly rates. The tables are in the served HTML, so the answer is
readable without running any JavaScript.

## What makes these figures citable

- Every rate names its source and the date it was read. Where a state's own law is the
  source, the statute is quoted verbatim rather than paraphrased.
- The assumptions are stated in full on the methodology page, along with an explicit list
  of what the calculators deliberately do not model.
- Where our figure and an official source disagree, the official source is correct and
  ours is a defect.

## State paycheck calculators

- [Washington paycheck calculator 2026](https://statelinecalc.com/paycheck-calculator/washington/): No state income tax on wages, but Paid Family and Medical Leave (employee share 0.807159% of wages up to $184,500) and WA Cares (0.58%, no cap) are withheld. Washington does levy a capital gains excise tax, which does not touch wages. A $75,000 single filer keeps about $60,552.
- [Nevada paycheck calculator 2026](https://statelinecalc.com/paycheck-calculator/nevada/): Nothing is withheld at state level. No income tax, no payroll programs, no disability or paid leave premium. A $75,000 single filer keeps about $61,593.
- [Texas paycheck calculator 2026](https://statelinecalc.com/paycheck-calculator/texas/): No income tax, and the ban is constitutional rather than statutory — Texas Constitution Article 8, Section 24-a. Section 24-b, added November 4, 2025, also prohibits a capital gains tax. Unemployment insurance is employer-only under Texas Labor Code Section 204.003. A $75,000 single filer keeps about $61,593.
- [Florida paycheck calculator 2026](https://statelinecalc.com/paycheck-calculator/florida/): Nothing is withheld at state level. The Florida Constitution, Article VII Section 5(a), caps rather than flatly bans a tax on the income of natural persons, which is a real difference from Texas even though the paycheck is identical. Reemployment tax is paid by employers on the first $7,000 of wages. A $75,000 single filer keeps about $61,593.
- [Illinois paycheck calculator 2026](https://statelinecalc.com/paycheck-calculator/illinois/): A flat 4.95% state income tax, unchanged since 2017. What you subtract first is a personal exemption of $2,925 counted per person, not a standard deduction per return, and it is not allowed at all above $250,000 of AGI ($500,000 filing jointly) - a cliff, not a taper, worth $144.79 to a single filer. A $75,000 single filer keeps about $58,025.
- [Georgia paycheck calculator 2026](https://statelinecalc.com/paycheck-calculator/georgia/): A flat 4.99% state income tax after a standard deduction of $15,000 single or $30,000 married filing jointly. Georgia did not conform to the federal treatment of tips and overtime for 2026: it exempts up to $1,750 of each, against $25,000 of qualified tips federally. A $75,000 single filer keeps about $58,599.
- [All states index](https://statelinecalc.com/paycheck-calculator/): Which states levy no income tax, and which calculators are live.

## Salary to hourly, after tax

Every other converter answers "$60,000 a year is how much an hour?" with $28.85, which is
just $60,000 divided by 2,080 and is the same in every state. These pages give the figure
that reaches the account, which is not: $24.23 an hour in Texas, $22.87 in Illinois.

- [Salary to hourly calculator, all states](https://statelinecalc.com/salary-to-hourly-calculator/): The same $60,000 converted in six states, before and after tax, side by side.
- [Texas](https://statelinecalc.com/salary-to-hourly-calculator/texas/), [Florida](https://statelinecalc.com/salary-to-hourly-calculator/florida/) and [Nevada](https://statelinecalc.com/salary-to-hourly-calculator/nevada/): $60,000 a year is $24.23 an hour after tax. No state withholding at all, so the figure is identical in the three.
- [Washington](https://statelinecalc.com/salary-to-hourly-calculator/washington/): $23.83 an hour after tax. No income tax, but two state payroll programs come out.
- [Georgia](https://statelinecalc.com/salary-to-hourly-calculator/georgia/): $23.15 an hour after tax, after a flat 4.99% state income tax.
- [Illinois](https://statelinecalc.com/salary-to-hourly-calculator/illinois/): $22.87 an hour after tax, after a flat 4.95% and a personal exemption of only $2,925.

Each state page carries a 30-row table converting salaries from $25,000 to $500,000, giving
the gross hourly rate, the after-tax hourly rate, and the yearly, monthly and weekly figures.

## Reference

- [Methodology](https://statelinecalc.com/methodology/): The exact formula, every 2026 federal figure with its official source and the date it was verified, and what the calculators deliberately do not model.
- [Disclaimer](https://statelinecalc.com/disclaimer/): Why an estimate will not match a pay stub to the dollar, and the eight most common reasons for the gap.
- [Privacy](https://statelinecalc.com/privacy/): Figures typed into a calculator never leave the browser. Google Analytics is the only third-party service loaded.

## Key 2026 federal figures used throughout

- Standard deduction: $16,100 single, $32,200 married filing jointly, $24,150 head of household.
- Federal brackets, single: 10% to $12,400, 12% to $50,400, 22% to $105,700, 24% to $201,775, 32% to $256,225, 35% to $640,600, 37% above.
- Social Security: 6.2% of wages up to a $184,500 wage base.
- Medicare: 1.45% of all wages, plus 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax above $200,000.
